raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-unified-memory` and the page-major layout, the GDN state pool pitches each slot wider than its state, so `conv_states` and `ssm_states` are strided views. `GDNAttnBackend.forward_extend` gathered every prefill's conv and recurrent states into packed copies, ran the kernels on them with identity indices, and scattered both back: two gathers, an arange and two scatters per GDN layer per prefill batch, whatever the batch's length (the `TODO(ch-wan)` in that code).

Two of the kernels that round trip protected already address slots by the pool's stride:
- GDN prefill reaches the Triton causal conv on CUDA and ROCm (a transposed input with host lengths), which takes every conv-state stride and offsets slots in int64; KDA hands its strided pool to the same kernel.
- FlashInfer's GDN prefill gathers each sequence's state by index and writes it back with `index_copy_`, so on a strided pool it ran a second gather and scatter on top of ours.

The Triton chunk kernel does not: `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` steps slots by `initial_state.stride(0)`, but its entry point, `ChunkGatedDeltaRuleFunction.forward`, is wrapped in FLA's `input_guard`, which makes every tensor argument contiguous. On a strided pool it would read the right states and write the final ones into a discarded copy.

## Modifications

- `LinearAttnKernelBase.extend_honors_slot_pitch` (default False): the kernel's `extend()` reads and writes each slot's state at the pool's own slot pitch. `FlashInferGDNKernel` sets it; `TritonGDNKernel` sets it False explicitly; other kernels keep the default.
- `GDNKernelDispatcher.extend_honors_slot_pitch` forwards the prefill kernel's flag.
- `forward_extend` skips the gather/scatter when the platform is CUDA or ROCm (the prefill conv then takes the Triton conv), the prefill kernel declares the flag, and each slot's own state is packed. Otherwise it keeps the packed copies, as before. The contiguous default pool never gathered and is unchanged.
- The page-major allowlist's note on FlashInfer prefill in `kv_cache_hook.py` now says why it is stride-safe on its own.

GDN prefill defaults to FlashInfer on SM90 and SM100 for supported configurations, so that is where this applies by default; with `--linear-attn-prefill-backend triton` (or wherever FlashInfer prefill is not chosen) the round trip stays.

Tests:
- `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_gdn_prefill_backend_policy.py` (CPU), `TestGDNPrefillOnStridedStatePool`: a strided pool prefills in place only when the prefill kernel follows the pitch, the platform is CUDA or ROCm and each slot is packed; the FlashInfer kernel declares the flag, and the Triton kernel and the base class do not. All three cases fail on main.
- `test/registered/attention/test_gdn_prefill_strided_state.py` (CUDA): the Triton conv and the FlashInfer prefill on a strided pool against a packed pool holding the same values: the same outputs and states, and the elements between slots untouched.

## Accuracy Tests

SM90, main `76d5b3ce02` with this PR, Qwen3.5-9B, TP 1, radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs on, GDN prefill on its default (FlashInfer, in place). sgl-eval GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, `--temperature 0 --max-tokens 2048 --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false`. The unified-memory servers ran with `SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL=1`, so a read of a never-written pool row shows up as a wrong answer.

| speculative decoding | attention backend | default pool | `--enable-unified-memory` | one pool only right (default / unified), p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | triton | 0.9505 | 0.9505 | 3 / 3, p = 1.00 |
| off | trtllm_mha | 0.9528 | 0.9513 | 2 / 0, p = 0.50 |
| NEXTN | triton | 0.9513 | 0.9513 | 3 / 3, p = 1.00 |
| NEXTN | trtllm_mha | 0.9521 | 0.9536 | 2 / 4, p = 0.69 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup. `python -m sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name random` with fixed input and output lengths. Each number is the unified-memory server against the default pool on the same commit, main / this PR; a second default-pool server gives the run-to-run spread in parentheses. The gain is small: it mostly shows in TTFT on the shorter prompts.

Without speculative decoding, `--attention-backend triton`:

| requests | input / output tokens | max concurrency | throughput gap, main / this PR | mean TTFT gap, main / this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | 1024 / 256 | 32 | -0.9% / -0.8% (1.9) | +3.4% / +1.3% (2.4) |
| 200 | 2048 / 512 | 64 | -1.1% / -0.5% (0.2) | +3.2% / +0.8% (0.5) |
| 100 | 8192 / 64 | 64 | -0.2% / -0.1% (0.0) | +0.9% / +0.1% (0.1) |

NEXTN (`--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`), `--attention-backend trtllm_mha`:

| requests | input / output tokens | max concurrency | throughput gap, main / this PR | mean TTFT gap, main / this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | 2048 / 512 | 64 | +0.1% / -0.3% (2.1) | +0.8% / +0.3% (0.9) |
| 100 | 8192 / 64 | 64 | -0.4% / -0.4% (0.1) | +1.0% / +0.6% (0.1) |

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

@@ -0,0 +1,125 @@
+"""GDN prefill kernels on an envelope-strided state pool.
+
+GDNAttnBackend runs prefill in place on a pool whose slots are pitched wider than
+their state (unified memory) when the conv and extend kernels follow that pitch.
+Each case runs a kernel on such a pool and on a packed pool holding the same
+values: outputs and states must match, and the bytes between slots stay untouched.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.mamba.causal_conv1d import causal_conv1d_fn
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+# Arbitrary; any gap breaks the packing.
+PAD = 7
+
+
+def envelope(pool: torch.Tensor):
+    """`pool`'s values with every slot PAD elements apart, NaN in between."""
+    slots, per_slot = pool.shape[0], pool[0].numel()
+    base = torch.full(
+        (slots, per_slot + PAD), float("nan"), dtype=pool.dtype, device=pool.device
+    )
+    view = base[:, :per_slot].view(pool.shape)
+    view.copy_(pool)
+    return view, base
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "Test requires CUDA")
+class TestGDNPrefillStridedStatePool(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        self.device = "cuda"
+        # Three sequences of unequal length on non-adjacent slots of six.
+        self.lens = [5, 17, 64]
+        self.cache_indices = torch.tensor(
+            [4, 0, 2], dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device
+        )
+        self.query_start_loc = torch.tensor(
+            [0, 5, 22, 86], dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device
+        )
+
+    def assert_same_pool(self, packed, strided, base):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(strided, packed)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.isnan(base[:, packed[0].numel() :]).all())
+
+    def gdn_inputs(self, qk_heads, v_heads, head_dim=128):
+        tokens, dtype = sum(self.lens), torch.bfloat16
+        q = torch.randn(1, tokens, qk_heads, head_dim, dtype=dtype, device=self.device)
+        k = torch.randn(1, tokens, qk_heads, head_dim, dtype=dtype, device=self.device)
+        v = torch.randn(1, tokens, v_heads, head_dim, dtype=dtype, device=self.device)
+        g = torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid(
+            torch.randn(1, tokens, v_heads, dtype=dtype, device=self.device)
+        )
+        beta = torch.sigmoid(
+            torch.randn(1, tokens, v_heads, dtype=dtype, device=self.device)
+        )
+        packed = (
+            torch.randn(
+                6, v_heads, head_dim, head_dim, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device
+            )
+            * 0.1
+        )
+        return (q, k, v, g, beta), packed
+
+    def check_extend(self, kernel, qk_heads, v_heads):
+        args, packed = self.gdn_inputs(qk_heads, v_heads)
+        strided, base = envelope(packed)
+        outputs = [
+            kernel.extend(
+                *args,
+                ssm_states=pool,
+                cache_indices=self.cache_indices,
+                query_start_loc=self.query_start_loc,
+            )[0]
+            for pool in (packed, strided)
+        ]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(outputs[1], outputs[0])
+        self.assert_same_pool(packed, strided, base)
+
+    def test_flashinfer_extend(self):
+        try:
+            from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kernels.gdn_flashinfer import (
+                FlashInferGDNKernel,
+            )
+
+            kernel = FlashInferGDNKernel()
+        except (ImportError, RuntimeError) as exc:
+            self.skipTest(f"FlashInfer GDN prefill is unavailable: {exc}")
+        self.check_extend(kernel, qk_heads=4, v_heads=8)
+
+    def test_triton_conv(self):
+        dim, width, dtype = 256, 4, torch.bfloat16
+        x = torch.randn(sum(self.lens), dim, dtype=dtype, device=self.device)
+        weight = torch.randn(dim, width, dtype=dtype, device=self.device)
+        bias = torch.randn(dim, dtype=dtype, device=self.device)
+        has_initial_state = torch.tensor([True, False, True], device=self.device)
+        packed = torch.randn(6, dim, width - 1, dtype=dtype, device=self.device)
+        strided, base = envelope(packed)
+        # GDN prefill hands the conv a transposed input and host lengths, which
+        # routes it to the Triton kernel.
+        outputs = [
+            causal_conv1d_fn(
+                x.transpose(0, 1),
+                weight,
+                bias,
+                activation="silu",
+                conv_states=pool,
+                has_initial_state=has_initial_state,
+                cache_indices=self.cache_indices,
+                query_start_loc=self.query_start_loc,
+                seq_lens_cpu=self.lens,
+            )
+            for pool in (packed, strided)
+        ]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(outputs[1], outputs[0])
+        self.assert_same_pool(packed, strided, base)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+class TestGDNPrefillOnStridedStatePool(CustomTestCase):
+    """An envelope-strided state pool prefills in place exactly when every prefill
+    kernel follows its slot pitch; otherwise prefill runs on packed copies."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def envelope_pool(slots=3, heads=2, v_dim=2, k_dim=2, pad=5):
+        # A [slots, H, V, K] state pool whose slots sit `pad` elements apart.
+        base = torch.zeros(slots, heads * v_dim * k_dim + pad)
+        return base[:, : heads * v_dim * k_dim].view(slots, heads, v_dim, k_dim)
+
+    @staticmethod

+        backend = object.__new__(GDNAttnBackend)
+        backend.kernel_dispatcher = SimpleNamespace(
+            extend_honors_slot_pitch=extend_honors_slot_pitch
+        )
+        return backend
+
+    def test_strided_pool_prefills_in_place_when_kernels_follow_the_pitch(self):
+        ssm_states = self.envelope_pool()
+        self.assertFalse(ssm_states.is_contiguous())
